subject: Run-rate audit & roll-forward plan for May renewal
messages:
From: Maya Lin <maya.lin@cobaltai.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 2 May 2027 08:14:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected run-rate increase ahead of renewal

Hi Soojin,

We're seeing an unplanned jump in inference tokens over the last 6 weeks — about a 68% lift month-over-month driven by our new summary feature. Renewal is up 5/15 and the finance team is asking for a quick consumption breakdown and any smoothing options you can propose.

Numbers (approx):
- Apr total tokens: 38.2M
- May projected (run-rate as of 5/2): 64.2M
- Peak daily: 3.8M tokens (2027-04-27)

Can your team run a short audit of token mix (chat v. batch), identify obvious tail tokens, and suggest term/commit options to avoid a surprise overage? We also need an ROI note for the summary feature (value metric: time saved / support tickets reduced).

Attaching my internal cost sensitivity note separately (will forward if helpful).

Thanks — Maya
Maya Lin
Head of Platform
Cobalt AI

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Maya Lin <maya.lin@cobaltai.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 2 May 2027 12:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected run-rate increase ahead of renewal

Thanks Maya — we dug in and I ran a quick token audit. High-level findings are attached (20270502-token-audit.csv). Key takeaways: 

- Spike source: ~72% of new tokens are from long-context chat sessions from the summary feature; average context length ~2.4k tokens.
- Batch jobs (end-of-day analytics) are stable and represent ~18% of token volume.
- Tail tokens: ~6% of tokens come from several outlier flows (feature preview + elastic testing) we can throttle.

Immediate recommendations (low friction):
- Apply prefix caching for summary templates — estimated 12–18% token reduction within 2 weeks.
- Short-term guardrail: cap max_context for the summary endpoint to 1.5k for non-premium users (expected 10–15% drop in run-rate w/o UX loss).
- For renewal: consider a 6-month stepped commit (60M -> 80M) with a burst corridor to cover peak days. This reduces unit cost by ~11% vs pay-as-you-go on current mix.

Karthik, adding you to propose pricing/term language and an initial roll-forward proposal. Maya — can we set a 30-min call tomorrow to walk through the CSV and proposed guardrails?

Attachments: 20270502-token-audit.csv (token-by-endpoint CSV, sampled logs)

Best,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Maya Lin <maya.lin@cobaltai.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 3 May 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected run-rate increase ahead of renewal

Maya / Soojin — quick price-side note and a draft proposal I'm attaching. Highlights: 

- Baseline: current monthly run-rate (pre-mitigation) ~64M tokens -> annualized impact if unchanged: ~$X (see attached PDF).
- Proposal A (conservative): 6-month stepped commit: 60M / month first 3 months -> 80M / month thereafter; includes 20% burst capacity at no extra charge for one-off spikes. Expected unit price = $0.00XX/token (11% lower than PAYG).
- Proposal B (aggressive): 12-month commitment at 75M/month with 30% burst credit and an additional 3% volume discount for auto-renew.

Operational options: autoscaling headroom gating, request-level token caps, and a short-term quota for preview features (we can implement feature flags to throttle without code changes).

ROI framing to help with procurement: for the summary feature we estimate a 24% reduction in manual support touches and a projected $75k savings in engineering time over 6 months at current usage — numbers in the attachment.

Next step: Maya, if procurement prefers smaller term exposure, Proposal A + the prefix caching + context cap gets you near-term cost parity and runway to measure impact before committing higher. I can join a procurement call on Wed 5/5 if that helps.

Attachments: redwood_rollforward_proposal_20270503.pdf

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Renewals and Expansion
Redwood Inference

From: Soojin Lee <soojin.lee@redwood.com>
To: Maya Lin <maya.lin@cobaltai.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 4 May 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Unexpected run-rate increase ahead of renewal — mutual action plan

Maya — quick recap and agreed next steps so procurement has a single document to review: 

1) Immediate (this week) — Redwood actions
- Enable prefix caching for summary templates (estimated 12–18% token reduction) — SOOJIN: actioned, rollout scheduled 5/5 Canary.
- Implement non-premium context cap at 1.5k tokens (feature flag) — KARTHIK: gated throttling plan by 5/6.
- Provide a 7-day burst buffer for May renewal window while changes ramp (no charge for first 7 days).

2) Near-term (30 days) — joint items
- Redwood to provide updated consumption report (token-by-flow) on 6 May.
- Cobalt to run internal UX test on summary fidelity at capped context and report qualitative loss.

3) Renewal terms recommended to procurement
- Option A: 6-month stepped commit (60M -> 80M) + 20% burst corridor, 11% unit discount.
- Option B: 12-month commit (75M/month) + 30% burst + 3% auto-renew discount (best unit economics).

Ask: Maya / Ravi — can procurement confirm preferred option by 5/10? Karthik and I will prepare the formal amendment and redlined SLA if you select Option A or B.

Quoted for clarity:
> "Apply prefix caching for summary templates — estimated 12–18% token reduction within 2 weeks."

I'll follow up with the official roll-forward PDF and the amended clause draft once you confirm which option procurement prefers. Happy to join the procurement call on Wed 5/5; Karthik is available for pricing/contract reads on that call as well.

Best regards,
Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Strategic Sales
Redwood Inference
Cell: (415) 555-0199
thread_summary: Customer reported a 68% run-rate spike driven by a new summary feature ahead of a 5/15 renewal. Redwood ran a token audit, recommended caching and a context cap, and proposed two roll-forward commit options (6-month stepped or 12-month commit) combined with a short burst corridor. Mutual action plan set; request for procurement decision by 2027-05-10.
